stance_basis: signs letter protesting more restrictive federal ORV regulations on Nevada public lands
summary: M. B. Gillespie is one of multiple signatories on a letter to the Bureau of Land Management in Elko, Nevada, protesting more restrictive federal regulations on off-road vehicles on federally owned land in Nevada. The letter argues that the rugged terrain and remote locations of lakes, reservoirs, and hunting areas in Nevada make four-wheel drive vehicles a practical necessity for outdoor recreation, and that the signatories feel they do no harm to the terrain. No agency response to this letter appears in the document window.
complaint_summary: M. B. Gillespie co-signs a letter protesting more restrictive federal ORV regulations in Nevada, arguing that four-wheel drive vehicles are a practical necessity for accessing remote hunting and fishing areas in the state's rugged terrain.

statement.text:
We wish to add our voice of protest to more restrictive regulations by the Federal Government of off road vehicles on federally owned land in the state of Nevada.
We have chosen to live in this large and sparsely populated area for the expressed purpose of being near free and open land areas and as you know we have less than one person per square mile in Nevada.
The terrain in northern and north eastern Nevada is so rugged it is almost an abstract to negotiate most of this area without four wheel drive vehicles.
The lakes and reserviors are in very remote areas, mostly without roads. Hunting and fishing is our most popular out door sport in Nevada. Deer and chuckar partridge country is located in the most rugged and remote sections of our state. Four wheel drive vehicles are virtually a must in the pursuit of this sport.
Flease consider these sports and our feelings that these are our sacred rights. We feel we do no harm to the terrain hunting in these rugged areas where we go for weeks without seeing another person.
